summary.name: SRE interview with Ben Treynor Sloss
summary.one_liner: An interview in which Google VP of Engineering Ben Treynor Sloss explains what Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) is, how it differs from traditional operations, and how it uses error budgets, hiring, and monitoring practices.
use_cases: Understanding how SRE teams differ from traditional operations
Setting reliability targets and error budgets for a service
Deciding how to staff and structure an SRE team
Designing monitoring that avoids alert fatigue
Reducing manual operational work through automation
summary.what_it_does: The page is a written interview transcript rather than a software tool. Ben Treynor Sloss describes SRE as operations work done by software engineers who automate manual tasks. He covers hiring a roughly 50-50 mix of software and systems engineers, a rule that SRE teams spend at least 50% of time on development, and quarterly service reviews to catch teams drifting into operations work. He explains the error budget model, where the product sets an availability target and the remaining unavailability is spent on launches, with launches frozen once the budget is used up. He also describes monitoring as three categories: alerts, tickets, and logging, with software rather than humans doing the interpretation.
notable: Error budget model: 100% is the wrong reliability target, and unavailability budget is spent on launches
Rule that SRE teams spend at least 50% of time on engineering development, enforced by quarterly reviews
Monitoring split into three outputs: alerts, tickets, and logs
Hiring bar kept at Google SWE standard, with a 50-50 mix of software and systems backgrounds
caveats: Describes Google's internal practices from around the time of the interview; it is not a current how-to guide
Opinion and experience of one Google executive, not a formal methodology
